Subject: Re: BrightHealth pilot — purchase route & next ops steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps for procurement alignment: 

1) Commercial route options we discussed:
   - Marketplace (AWS GovCloud listing) — faster onboarding but requires marketplace billing approval from your procurement team.
   - Direct purchase (PO) — Redwood provides invoice + net-30 terms; your AP team issues PO.
   - Card (procurement card) — fastest for pilot but requires billing profile and card setup.

2) What we need from your side to unblock: 
   - Confirmation of preferred purchase channel (marketplace / PO / card)
   - Point person in procurement for vendor form and invoice routing (name + email)
   - Any required SOW or PO formatting your AP needs (we can provide a template)

Attachments I've included: Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf (pilot scope) and vendor-form.xlsx (vendor intake).

Proposed timeline if we get channel confirmed this week: 
- Day 0–2: legal / vendor form exchange
- Day 3–5: AP issues PO or confirms card setup
- Day 5–10: provisioning + kickoff

Can you confirm who will own the vendor intake? If procurement prefers I can loop Ben from Sales Ops to expedite the paperwork.

Best,

Hi Vivek — appreciated the recap. A few notes from procurement: 

- Marketplace would be preferable from our platform team perspective, but procurement needs to confirm marketplace vendor registration and whether this is allowable for a pilot. That can take 7–10 business days.
- PO is the fallback. We typically require vendor forms (W9, vendor setup spreadsheet) + a signed SOW.
- Card is acceptable for <$25k pilots but needs AP approval and a billing contact.

Action items from our side: 
- I'll ping procurement to nominate a point person — likely Rajiv or a procurement associate.
- Can you share a short plain-English SOW and the vendor form filled with Redwood's legal name and tax info?

Thanks — I'll loop back once I have a firm channel decision.

—Elena
